answer: Nullifier uniqueness stops batch forgery: each hardware credential yields exactly one zero-knowledge nullifier. The key stays private, the nullifier public; a reused nullifier is rejected on sight, and a sybil farm spirals into rejection as duplicates are refused. Each nullifier is carved in marble: permanent, singular. Forging 1,000 identities needs 1,000 keys at ~$25 each: $25,000 sunk cost, linear in N — an honest agent pays $25 once. A collision leaves a pigment stain on the record and triggers a slash; honesty stays cheapest, rewards undiluted.
